# Conformance corpus

<!-- Generated by scripts/render_corpus.py from tests/corpus: do not edit. -->

Schemas and CBOR from the RFCs and IETF drafts that use CDDL (RFC 8610 and RFC 9165 constructs, COSE, CoRIM, CoSWID, EDHOC, SUIT), each with the verdict its source gives, the constructs it exercises and where it came from. `tests/test_corpus.py` runs every case, so this page cannot describe behaviour the library does not have. The construct-by-construct view is the [conformance matrix](CONFORMANCE.md); this is the same question asked with real schemas.

605 cases in 7 suites. Cases that the library disagrees with are not hidden: each one carries a status and a reason, and keeps failing the test until the disagreement goes away (see *Statuses*).

## Statuses

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `pass` | this library gives the verdict of the source |
| `gap` | the library is wrong or does not do it yet: there is an issue, and the case keeps failing until it is fixed |
| `divergence` | the library differs on purpose, for the reason given |
| `source-defect` | the source's own schema or example is wrong, for the reason given; the library is right |

## Provenance

| Provenance | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `verbatim` | schema text and data bytes exactly as published |
| `converted` | published in diagnostic notation (EDN) and converted to CBOR with `cbor-diag` |
| `derived` | a published example changed in one stated way (a field removed, a tag changed, ...) |
| `adapted` | published text with rules added to make it usable (an adapter that wraps a sequence in an array, a stand-in for a module that is not bundled) |
| `constructed` | written for this corpus from the rules of the schema or section named |

## Known gaps, divergences and source defects

| Suite | Status | Issue | Cases | Why |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `cddlc-tests` | `divergence` |  | `cddlc/13a-size/01`, `cddlc/13a-size/02`, `cddlc/13a-size/04` and 1 more | RFC 8610 §3.8.1 defines `.size` for byte strings, text strings and unsigned integers; this library does not accept `int` as the target of `.size` (`uint .size N` works), where cddlc applies it to the non-negative integers. |
| `cddlc-tests` | `divergence` |  | `cddlc/16-feature/05`, `cddlc/16a-feature/05` | RFC 9165 leaves which features are enabled to the tool; this library has no way to name them, so every `.feature` counts as enabled and the base type alone decides. |
| `cddlc-tests` | `divergence` |  | `cddlc/6-bigint/03`, `cddlc/6-bigint/04`, `cddlc/6-bigint/05` | The RFC 8610 prelude defines `bigint = biguint / bignint` (tags 2 and 3 only) and this library follows it: an integer that fits in 64 bits is an `int` or `integer`, not a `bigint`. The cddlc test also accepts such integers. |

## Unsupported constructs

The constructs the [conformance matrix](CONFORMANCE.md) marks unsupported or partial, and whether the corpus has a case that shows it. A case marked `gap` is a schema and data the source says are valid (or invalid) that the library gets wrong because the construct is not enforced.

| Construct | Matrix status | Corpus cases | Showing the gap |
|---|---|--:|--:|
| `mime-message` | partial | none |  |

## Layout

```
tests/corpus/
  suites/<suite>.json    the cases of one suite, with its sources
  schemas/               the CDDL files the cases name (published text, kept unchanged)
tests/_corpus.py         loads and runs the corpus
tests/test_corpus.py     checks the format and runs every case
scripts/build_corpus.py  rebuilds the suites from clones of the upstream repositories
scripts/render_corpus.py writes this page
```

A suite names its `sources` (name, URL, commit, licence), its `schema` (one file or a list that is joined), its `modules` (name to file, for `;# import`) and `provenance`. A case has:

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `id` | unique name |
| `hex` | the CBOR, in hexadecimal (absent for a `schema-error` case) |
| `edn` | the published diagnostic notation `hex` was converted from, when there was one |
| `expect` | what the source says: `valid`, `invalid`, or `schema-error` (the schema itself is refused) |
| `status` | `pass` (the default) or why the library differs |
| `issue`, `reason` | the issue a `gap` waits on; the reason for a `gap`, `divergence` or `source-defect` |
| `constructs` | ids of the rows of the conformance matrix the case exercises |
| `source` | where in the source the case comes from, or what was changed to derive it |
| `provenance` | see above; on the suite when every case shares it |
| `schema`, `root`, `modules` | override the suite's; `root` defaults to the first rule |
| `encoding` | `sequence` for a CBOR sequence (RFC 8742): the items are checked as the array `root` describes |
| `deterministic` | check with `require_deterministic` (RFC 8949 §4.2.1) |
| `note` | anything else worth knowing |

## Adding or updating cases

- A case from a new source: add a builder to `scripts/build_corpus.py` (clone the source, record its commit and licence, take the schema and data from it) and run `python scripts/build_corpus.py --sources DIR`. The script stops on a case the library disagrees with that nothing explains.
- A library fix that makes a `gap` or `divergence` case agree: the test fails on it. Remove the explanation in `scripts/build_corpus.py`, rebuild, and run `python scripts/render_corpus.py`.
- Run the corpus: `python -m pytest tests/test_corpus.py`.
